title: Public Notice
text: -PUBLIC NOTICEAmelia County Board of Supervisors At its rescheduled regular meeting beginning at 7:00pm on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, in the Conference Room at the Amelia County Administration Building located at 16360 Dunn Street Amelia Court House, VA 23002, the Amelia County Board of Supervisors will consider the following proposed ordinances for adoption: Ordinance to amend the County Code to establish the Amelia County Department of Fire and EMS Services. Ordinance to amend the County Code to update current Emergency Management provisions. Ordinance to amend the County Code to update the Amelia Sanitary District Cross-Connection provisions. Copies of the full text of the proposed ordinances are available for public inspection at the County Administration office located at 16360 Dunn Street Amelia, Va 23002. If you have any questions, please contact County Administration at 804-561-3039 or email at info@ameliacova.com.

The Comprehensive Plan suggests the property is appropriate for Rural Residential/Agricultural (0.2 units per acre or less) use. Tax ID 746-6525294. H. 26SN2253: In Matoaca Magisterial District, Hull Street Road Telecommunication Tower is a request for conditional use to permit a telecommunication tower and amendment of zoning district map in an Agricultural (A) District on 0.25 acre known as 23101 Hull Street Road. The Comprehensive Plan suggests the property is appropriate for Rural Residential/Agricultural (0.2 units per acre or less) use. Tax ID 677-654-Part of 8486. I. 26SN2256: In Matoaca Magisterial District, Automotive Concepts Rezoning and Adjustments is a request to rezone from Agricultural (A) to Corridor Commercial (CC) with adjustments to ordinance requirements plus conditional use to permit an automobile repair use and amendment of zoning district map on 3.75 acres fronting approximately 150 feet on the south side of Hull Street Road, 690 feet west of Doss Road, known as 18619 Hull Street Road. The Comprehensive Plan suggests the property is appropriate for Rural Residential/Agricultural use. Tax ID 699-664-0591. Action on Comprehensive Plan Modernization "PlanMod" Amendment 26PJ0006 PlanMod is an amendment to Moving Forward - The Comprehensive Plan for Chesterfield. Virginia law requires that all local governments adopt, and periodically update, their comprehensive plan. The Plan does not rezone property or change uses or densities of property. The amendment includes updates and revisions to language, data, charts, tables, maps and graphics throughout the entire Plan, including but not limited Chesterfield County Planning Commission Meeting November 17, 2026 to updates to the Land Use Plan and Thoroughfare Plan maps. Some of the chapters of the Plan have been renamed or renumbered. The proposed draft Land Use Plan Map reflects how the county is growing and changing to better align with existing development patterns, current market conditions, and the natural character of different parts of the county. Generally, the proposed changes to the Land Use Plan map include: lowering residential densities south and west of Route 288; reducing areas designated with the mixed-use categories; reducing areas designated with Office, Light Production & Assembly; and updating the Conservation/Recreation and Institutional designations to meet the new criteria outlined within these categories. The Land Use Plan serves as guide for zoning, land use and development decisions, but does not rezone or regulate property. The Planning Commission held a public hearing on October 20, 2026, on the Comprehensive Plan Amendment - Comprehensive Plan Modernization "PlanMod", and after taking public comment, closed the public hearing. Action on the Comprehensive Plan Amendment for the Comprehensive Plan Modernization "PlanMod" was deferred until the November 17, 2026, Planning Commission meeting. 15. The meeting may also be viewed on the City's streaming platforms and local government Channel 10. Individuals with disabilities who require assistance or special arrangements to participate in the public meeting may call (434) 987-1267 or submit a request via email to ada@charlottesville.gov. The City of Charlottesville requests that you provide 48 hours’ notice so that proper arrangements may be made. • The presiding officer shall ensure that individuals address their comments to City Council at appropriate times, in accordance with the meeting agenda and Council’s Rules of Procedure. • No person who is not a member of the city council shall orally address it until leave to do so has been granted by the city council or until invited to do so by the mayor. (City Code sec.2-71) • Remarks and actions that disrupt the progress of the Council meeting, and remarks from persons other than councilors, the City Manager, the City Attorney, or a presenter for an Agenda Item are not permitted. • The presiding officer shall call an individual to order, including a councilor, when that individual goes afoul of these rules. The following are examples of remarks and behavior that are not permitted: • i. Interrupting a speaker who is addressing Council at the speaker's microphone, or interrupting a speaker who has otherwise been invited to address Council during Community Matters or a Public Hearing ii. Interrupting a councilor who is speaking iii. Shouting, and talking (either individually or in concert with others) in a manner that prevents a speaker or a Councilor from being heard or that otherwise hinders the progress of the meeting iv. Blocking paths for emergency exit from the meeting room; engaging in any conduct that prevents a member of the audience from seeing or hearing councilors during a meeting; standing on chairs or tables within the Council meeting room v. Threats or incitement of violence toward councilors, City staff or members of the public vi. Engaging in conduct that is a criminal offense under the City Code or the Virginia Code vii. Campaigning for elected office viii. Promotion of private business ventures ix. Using profanity or vulgarity x. Personal attacks against Councilors, City staff or members of the public xi. Behavior which tends to intimidate others During a City Council meeting the presiding officer shall have control of the Council Chambers and the connecting halls and corridors within City Hall, and any other venue where a Council meeting is being held. In case of any conduct described above, the presiding officer may take measures deemed appropriate, including but not limited to suspending the meeting until order is restored, ordering areas to be cleared by the Sergeant at Arms, or requiring any individual to exit the meeting room and adjacent premises (connecting halls and corridors.)

text: City of Petersburg Planning Commission Meeting Agenda Thursday, November 5, 2026 6:00 PM Petersburg Public Library 1. Call to Order 2. Roll Call 3. Adoption of the Agenda 4. Consent Agenda a. October 1, 2026 Regular Meeting Minutes (pages 3-10) b. October 26, 2026 Special Meeting Minutes (pages 11-17) 5. Public Comment Comments and Correspondence from citizens, visitors, and delegations in the audience on items not on the agenda. Individuals wishing to speak should sign up prior to the start of the meeting. Please limit comments to no more than three minutes. Total Public Comment period shall not exceed 15 minutes. 6. Public Hearings a. 2026-SUP-06: Consideration of a resolution recommending approval of a request by Lawrence Ellis Williams Consulting LLC, on behalf of SP-Thirteen Properties LLC, for a special use permit to operate an assisted living facility at 36 West Fillmore Street, Parcel ID 022360001, in the RB Office-Apartment Zoning District (pages 18-88) 7. Old Business 1 a. Discussion and review of Planning Commission Bylaws (pages 89-97) b. ZONING AND SUBDIVISION ORDINANCE AMENDMENT AND READOPTION: The City’s Zoning Ordinance is proposed to be holistically repealed and replaced with a reorganized and updated Zoning/Subdivision Ordinance. The proposed Ordinance reorganizes articles and standards; contains technical language changes to ease interpretation/application and to follow the most current Code of Virginia regulations; modifies dimensional standards for the City’s primary zoning districts; and changes permitted land uses within zoning districts that include, but are not limited to, deletion and addition of uses and categorization of certain uses into broader terms, and including additional and modified definitions of terms accordingly. The updated ordinance may be adopted with a delayed effective date. (pages 98-108) Full Draft Ordinance available for viewing at http://www.petersburgva.org/DocumentCenter/View/9088/Draft-Ordinance---1012026?bidId= Individual Articles available for viewing at http://www.petersburg-va.org/688/CurrentProjects 8. New Business 9. Secretary/City Staff Reports a. Update on City Council public hearing actions a. 2026-COMP-01 and 2026-REZ-05; Tabled until December meeting b. 2026-SUP-04; Tabled until January meeting c. 2026-REZ-06; Approved as submitted d. 2026-REZ-06; Denied as presented 10. Announcements/Commissioner Reports 11. Adjournment 2 City of Petersburg Planning Commission Meeting Minutes October 1, 2026 Members Present: Marshall Ford, Chair (arrived at 6:03 p.m.) Alvin Cannon, Vice-Chair (arrived at 6:06 p.m.) Fenton Bland Kirsten Katzenbach Aku Reinhardt (arrived at 6:04 p.m.) James Norman Tony McDaniel Dianne Harley Members Absent: Thomas Hairston Others Present: Jared Crews, City Planning Staff Elaine Negasi, City Planning Staff 1. Call to Order: The City of Petersburg Planning Commission meeting held on Thursday, October 1, 2026, was called to order by Mr. Crews at 6:00 p.m. Commissioner Norman was elected to serve as chair (Chair Ford arrived at 6:02 and took over) on motion Commissioner Katzenbach, seconded by Commissioner Harley. 2. Roll Call: A quorum was established by Ms. Negasi. Chair Ford, Vice-Chair Cannon, and Commissioner Aku arrived following the roll call. 3. Adoption of the Agenda: Chair Ford arrived and assumed directing the meeting. Commissioner Bland motioned to approve the agenda, which included an additional discussion on potential updates to the Planning Commission bylaws. Commissioner Norman seconded the motion, which passed unanimously. 3 4. Consent Agenda: Commissioner Katzenbach motioned to approve the consent agenda, which included changes to the minutes of the September 3, 2026 meeting to reflect her concern that the proposed apartments on Graham Road should match the scale and character of the surrounding development. Commissioner Bland seconded the motion, which passed unanimously. 5. Public Comment: Chair Ford opened the floor for public comment. Hearing no comments, the public comment period was closed. 6. Public Hearings: a. ZONING AND SUBDIVISION ORDINANCE AMENDMENT AND READOPTION: The City’s Zoning Ordinance is proposed to be holistically repealed and replaced with a reorganized and updated Zoning/Subdivision Ordinance. The proposed Ordinance reorganizes articles and standards; contains technical language changes to ease interpretation/application and to follow the most current Code of Virginia regulations; modifies dimensional standards for the City’s primary zoning districts; and changes permitted land uses within zoning districts that include, but are not limited to, deletion and addition of uses and categorization of certain uses into broader terms, and including additional and modified definitions of terms accordingly. The updated ordinance may be adopted with a delayed effective date. Tori Haynes, the Berkeley Group, was present to provide a project summary on the draft zoning ordinance and the review process so far. Ms. Haynes provided an overview of the eleven draft articles and laid out the remaining steps in the adoption process. Ms. Haynes noted several mandatory laws were passed at the state level that were incorporated into the draft ordinance. Chair Ford opened the floor to public comment. Michael Packer, 1245 Woodland Road, presented a PowerPoint outlining his concern regarding the ordinance update. Mr. Packer stated his concern regarding the reduced minimum lot area and width in several districts within the new ordinance. Mr. Packer stated the new ordinance would require a zoning permit for structures not previously required and he does not believe the new rule can be properly enforced by the Zoning Administrator. Mr. Packer stated he believed the new zoning ordinance would allow the Zoning Administrator the ability to classify an unlisted use as similar to a listed use, which 4 Mr. Parker argued will give the Zoning Administrator legislative authority to grant uses not permitted under state law. Mr. Parker stated there should be an updated zoning map along with the new ordinance since substantial changes are being proposed. Mr. Parker requested the Planning Commission to give additional time for Commission, staff, and the consultant to revise the draft zoning ordinance before sending their recommendation to City Council. Leonard Curry, 2014 Woodland Road, stated Delectable Heights and Ward 1 had existing 25-foot width lots and he did not think that the new lot standard would expand into other neighborhoods. Mr. Curry mentioned concern about the increase in infill development that residents did not anticipate during the previous public comment periods. Richard Taylor, 828 W Tuckahoe Street spoke on his concern regarding the traffic increase related to the possible high-density residential development. Gennie Parker, 628 Bradford Lane, stated he would like some clarity on the Faith in Housing Act and how multi-family dwelling units will be incorporated on properties. Mr. Parker asked if multi-family housing would be allowed in single-family housing districts. Marlo Green, 301 Rolfe Street, stated the new changes to lot requirements will modernize the city. Ms. Green stated the decreased lot size requirements are similar standards to other cities in the region and will attract residents to move into the city. Ms. Hayes responded to the concerns presented by the public comments. Ms. Hayes stated Berkeley Group was originally directed to create a form-based code for the draft zoning ordinance with the anticipation that an updated zoning map would be incorporated. Ms. Haynes stated that following a rejection of this proposal by City Council, Berkeley Group worked with staff to incorporate changes within the existing zoning districts with some form-based components. Ms. Hayes stated Berkeley Group identified underutilized lots as a key issue, so the 25-foot lot width minimum in some districts was developed as a solution because it reflected the existing development patterns. Ms. Haynes stated the smaller lot sizes were also proposed as a solution to the missing middle housing in single-family districts. Ms. Haynes stated the Faith in Housing Act is mandatory was adopted by the state and allows multi-family and some mixed-use development on properties owned by religious or tax exempt entities. Ms. Haynes explained that as long as a proposed development met certain criteria for providing affordable housing, these developments are considered by-right. Ms. Haynes clarified that Virginia is a Dillon rule state, meaning localities do not 5 have the ability to pass local laws in contradiction with state law, and the requirements of the Faith in Housing Act would be mandatory for all localities throughout the state. Chair Ford asked the Commission if they have any questions. Commissioner Katzenbach stated she had the same concerns as the speakers in the audience. Commissioner Bland stated the Commission will require more time to dissect the draft ordinance. Chair Ford agreed with Commissioner Bland. Mr. Crews stated if the Commission is requesting additional time to review the draft ordinance, they will need to commit seriously to that process. Mr. Crews reminded the Commission that the rewrite of the ordinance has been ongoing since 2024 and several work sessions were held over the last 18-months to review the draft articles. Mr. Crews noted that attendance at those meetings was poor and very little feedback was received on the draft. Mr. Crews also emphasized that there are several updates that are mandatory from State law so the City will need to move forward with updates in a timely fashion. Chair Ford requested a special Planning Commission meeting this month to discuss the ordinance update and stated he would coordinate with Mr. Crews to set a date. Commissioner Aku stated he agreed with Chair Ford and suggested a sub-committee should be formed. Commissioner Katzenbach stated members of the public should be involved in the sub-committee. Commissioner Bland motioned for the deferral of action on the Zoning Ordinance rewrite and request to set up special meeting to review draft ordinance. Commissioner Katzenbach seconded the motion, which passed unanimously. Marlo Green asked how members of the public will be selected and how will the decisions be held accountable. Ms. Green stated if a sub-committee will be formed then the Commission should be held accountable to attend each meeting. b. 2026-REZ-05: Consideration of a resolution recommending approval of an amendment to the Zoning Ordinance of the City of Petersburg for the purpose of introducing additional Zoning regulations pertaining to data center uses, including a special use permit requirement. Mr. Crews provided background on this amendment to introduce additional zoning regulations to data center uses. Mr. Crews stated prior to January 2025, a former Zoning Administrator made a decision that data centers were similar to a general warehouse 6 use and were given by-right in Industrial districts. Mr. Crews stated two data center developments located on Jamestown Drive and Wagner Road submitted site plans under this interpretation. Mr. Crews stated by January 2025, Staff worked with Planning Commission and City Council to draft regulations on data centers as a specific use. Mr. Crews stated City Council adopted data center regulations in the Zoning Ordinance on January 21, 2025. An additional property was rezoned with intent to construct a data center development (Collier Yard), and one additional site plan was submitted for byright development (County Drive); a total of four data centers presently. Mr. Crews stated H.B. 153 and S.B. 94 were signed into law this year, giving localities additional powers to require site assessments for data center uses and Governor Spanberger signed Executive Order 22 establishing standards and initiatives for “data center” accountability framework. Mr. Crews stated data centers are allowed as a by-right use in the M-1, Light Industrial, and M-2, Heavy Industrial, districts with specific requirements for setbacks and vegetative buffers for properties adjoining residential development. Mr. Crews stated new information continues to become available about the impact of data centers (noise, energy and water demands, heat, etc.); several localities have moved from allowing data centers by-right to requiring special use permits or allowing them only in specific overlay areas. Mr. Crews stated the proposed amendment will require a Special-Use Permit and reclassify the use from by-right to special use in M-1, Light Industrial, and M-2, Heavy Industrial, districts with automatic conditions and application requirements. Mr. Crews stated applicants will be required to hold a community meeting prior to a formal public hearing, to allow questions and feedback from neighboring property owners. Mr. Crews stated the applicant would need to provide a summary of input received and written comments during the formal hearing process. Mr. Crews stated any new applications or modifications of existing facilities must provide a site assessment for consideration in accordance to the new state law. Mr. Crews stated Wendy Austin submitted a written comment prior to the hearing in favor for the increased minimum setbacks, buffers, and monitoring the impacts of data centers. Mr. Crews stated Ms. Austin recommended an increase to 300 feet in setbacks for mechanical equipment and operations between data centers and neighborhoods and an increase minimum vegetated buffer to 100-150 feet. Mr. Crews stated Ms. Austin recommended Livestreaming be required for community meetings and to add lighting and visual impact, and traffic & diesel delivery impact to the required site assessment. Mr. Crews stated a written comment from Eric Olson and Burt Cutright of 1200 Acqua LLC, who own and operate Acqua Apartments was received prior to the hearing. Mr. 7 Crews stated Acqua LLC are in favor to the amendment to the data center regulations, and requested additional sound studies. Mr. Crews stated any changes to the City’s Noise Ordinance would occur separate to the Zoning Ordinance and would need approval from City Council. Joyce Vinson, 1608 Kings Road, stated she believes the amendment addressed most of her concerns, but suggested Planning Commission consider a 500-foot setback from residential buildings and an annual noise study requirement every five years. Ms. Vinson stated any noise study results should be available to the public. Ms. Vinson asked for Staff to provide some clarity on the assessment language regarding voltage. Ms. Vinson requested this amendment be adopted by City Council for October. Marlo Green asked whether a community benefit agreement could be required to be provided with any data center application, so any development can actively serve community members. Michael Edwards, 409 Grove Avenue, stated the City’s limited land, resources, and infrastructure capacities cannot handle the high-intensity infrastructure uses of a data center. Mr. Edwards stated the city should not have to experience the issues related to data centers first and regulate later. Commissioner Katzenbach stated she had the same concerns as the speakers in the audience. Commissioner Katzenbach stated individual testing should be required by the ordinance and clarity needed on lighting infrastructure. Commissioner Katzenbach asked if the Collier Yard data center will require a special-use permit or would it be considered grandfathered in. Mr. Crews stated Collier Yard received the rezoning approval to prepare the land for data center development, but have not submitted a site plan for data center development. Mr. Crews stated he will consult with the Zoning Administrator and City Attorney for clarification on whether a vested interest had been established. Commissioner Katzenbach motioned for the approval of the text amendment as drafted. Commissioner Bland seconded the motion, which passed unanimously. 7. Old Business: a. 2026-SUP-03: Consideration of a resolution recommending approval of a request by Joe Tyler, Tyler Realty Group, on behalf of TAP LLC, for a special use permit for multiplefamily dwellings as authorized and controlled by the R-5 Multiple Dwelling District 8 Standards at 2719 South Crater Road, Parcel ID 065120007, in the B-2 General Commercial District. Mr. Crews presented the updated staff report regarding the request and stated the applicant was not able to attend the hearing. Mr. Crews stated no modifications were submitted to Staff from the last hearing. Mr. Crews stated the applicant submitted a letter asking for a favorable recommendation and that he understands the comprehensive plan does not support ground floor residential development on South Crater Road. Mr. Crews stated the applicant stated his request is based on his practical experience of leasing the property and his difficulty in finding a dependable commercial tenant. Mr. Crews stated the applicant believes reinvestment, improved appearance and professional management would contribute positively to the corridor. Mr. Crews stated Staff recommendation has not changed and ground floor residential is not compatible the Comprehensive Plan designation and the site plan does not include sufficient amenities or greenspace. Commissioner Bland motioned for the denial of the Special Use Permit request for 2719 South Crater Road based on lack of compatibility with the guidance of the Comprehensive Plan and the site constraints identified by staff. Vice-Chair Cannon seconded the motion, which passed unanimously. 8. New Business: a. Discussion on Proposed Bylaw Amendment Commissioner Aku stated presented proposed revisions to the current bylows and stated his recommendations were based on previous conversation between the Commission. Commissioner Aku stated the proposed amendment is to establish attendance standards, mandatory vacancy declaration, changes in applicant, FOIA availability, optional virtual meetings and interested witnesses’ presentation times. Commissioner Katzenbach asked to define certain terminology in the amendment and suggested the City Attorney clarify legal definitions. Mr. Crews stated a separate virtual attendance policy would need to be adopted by the Commission in addition to the bylaws if they are interested in introducing that option. Chair Ford stated City Council should provide input to the recommendation. The Commission discussed compensation for meeting attendance and Chair Ford noted that he was preparing a letter for City Council to address the Commissions concerns. 9 9. Secretary/City Staff Reports: No reports presented. Adjournment: The meeting was adjourned at 7:58 p.m. on motion by Commissioner Hairston, seconded by Commissioner Bland. _ Planning Commission Chair ___ Date 10 City of Petersburg Planning Commission Special Meeting Minutes October 26, 2026 Members Present: Marshall Ford, Chair Alvin Cannon, Vice-Chair (arrived at 6:08 p.m.) Fenton Bland Kirsten Katzenbach Aku Reinhardt James Norman Dianne Harley Thomas Hairston Members Absent: Tony McDaniel Others Present: Jared Crews, City Planning Staff Elaine Negasi, City Planning Staff 1. Call to Order: The City of Petersburg special Planning Commission meeting held on Monday, October 26, 2026, was called to order by Chair Ford at 6:05 p.m. 2. Roll Call: A quorum was established by Ms. Negasi. Vice-Chair Cannon arrived following the roll call. 3. Adoption of the Agenda: Commissioner Norman motioned to approve the agenda. Commissioner Hairston seconded the motion, which passed unanimously. Commissioner Bland asked if there would be a citizens committee present during the hearing. Mr. Crews stated this meeting is for the planning commission to review and discuss the questions regarding the zoning ordinance rewrite, and he had spoken to Chair Ford about establishing a subcommittee in the future, if needed. title: City Council Agenda
text: City of Roanoke, Virginia CITY COUNCIL INFORMAL SESSION November 2, 2026 9:00 AM City Council Chamber 215 Church Avenue, SW AGENDA The City of Roanoke is a safe, caring and economically vibrant community in which to live, learn, work, play and prosper. A vibrant urban center with strong neighborhoods set amongst the spectacular beauty of Virginia's Blue Ridge. NOTICE: City Council meetings will be televised live and replayed on RVTV Channel 3 on Thursdays at 7:00 pm, and Saturdays from 10:00 am to 5:00 pm; and video streamed through YouTube Live at youtube.com/RoanokeVa. Council meetings are offered with closed captioning for the deaf or hard of hearing. CALL TO ORDER - ROLL CALL. Welcome ITEMS FOR ACTION: A communication from Mayor Joseph L. Cobb requesting that the Council convene in a Closed Meeting to discuss vacancies on certain authorities, boards, commissions and committees appointed by the Council, pursuant to Section 2.2-3711 (A)(1), Code of Virginia (1950), as amended. • Architectural Review Board • City Planning Commission • Roanoke Arts Commission • Board of Zoning Appeals • Economic Development Authority • Fair Housing Board • Gun Violence Prevention Commission • Human Services Advisory Board • Roanoke Neighborhood Advocates • Roanoke Public Library Board • Towing Advisory Board A communication from Mayor Joseph L. Cobb, Chair, Roanoke City Council Personnel Committee, requesting that Council convene in a Closed Meeting to discuss annual performance evaluations of Council-Appointed Officers, pursuant to Section 2.2-3711 (A)(1), Code of Virginia (1950), as amended. A communication from Mayor Joseph L. Cobb requesting that Council convene in a Closed Meeting to discuss the 2026 Citizen of the Year Award, pursuant to Section 2.2-3711 (A)(10), Code of Virginia (1950), as amended. A communication from the City Attorney requesting that City Council convene in a closed meeting to consult with legal counsel pertaining to actual litigation regarding a status update, where such consultation or briefing in open meeting would adversely affect the negotiating or litigating posture of the public body, pursuant to Section 2.23711 (A)(7), Code of Virginia. Items listed on the 2:00 pm City Council docket requiring discussion/clarification and addition/deletions to the 2:00 pm agenda. (5 MINUTES) Topics for discussion by the Mayor and Members of City Council. (5 MINUTES) BRIEFING: Western Virginia Water Authority - Water Supply Study Results - 30 minutes LEGISLATIVE COMMITTEE MEETING SCHEDULED FOR 9:00 am, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER. THE COUNCIL MEETING WILL STAND IN RECESS FOR A CLOSED MEETING; AND THEREAFTER RECONVENE AT 2:00 pm, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER, ROOM 450, NOEL C. TAYLOR MUNICIPAL BUILDING. City of Roanoke, Virginia CITY COUNCIL 2:00 pm City Council Chamber 215 Church Avenue, SW 1. CALL TO ORDER - ROLL CALL. The Invocation will be delivered by The Reverend Amy Hodge, Pastor, Mt. Zion AME Church. The Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag of the United States of America will be led by Mayor Joseph L. Cobb. Welcome Certification of Closed Meeting. ANNOUNCEMENTS: 2. PRESENTATIONS AND ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS: Presentation by Elevate 11. Presentation by the Hope and Home Taskforce. 3. HEARING OF CITIZENS UPON PUBLIC MATTERS: The City Council sets this time as a priority for citizens to be heard. All matters will be referred to the City Manager for response, recommendation or report to the Council, as she may deem appropriate. 4. CONSENT AGENDA: C-1. Minutes of the regular meetings of City Council held on Monday, September 21, 2026, and on Monday, October 5, 2026. RECOMMENDED ACTION: Dispense with the reading of the minutes and approve as recorded. C-2. Request to schedule and advertise a public hearing to be held on Monday, November 16, 2026, at 7:00 pm, or as soon thereafter as the matter may be heard, to consider a tax exemption on real property owned by Roanoke Area Ministries. RECOMMENDED ACTION: Concur in the request. C-3. Request to schedule and advertise a public hearing to be held on Monday, November 16, 2026, at 7:00 pm or as soon as thereafter as the matter may be heard, to consider a request from Roanoke Gas Company for a utility easement along city-owned property located at 304 Reserve Avenue, SW, bearing Tax Map Number 1040202. RECOMMENDED ACTION: Concur in the request. C-4. Community Meeting announcement to seek public review and comment on the proposed draft update of City Code Chapter 11.8 Erosion and Stormwater Management to be held on Thursday, November 19, 2026, from 3:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. at the City of Roanoke Main Library, 706 S. Jefferson Street, Roanoke, VA 24016. RECOMMENDED ACTION: Receive and file. C-5. Report of qualifications of the following individuals: Anita Price as a member of the Youth Services Citizen Board for a two-year term of office commencing July 1, 2026, and ending June 30, 2028; Kristin Leary as a member of the Gun Violence Prevention Commission for a term of office ending March 31, 2029; Jonathan Pait as a member of the Youth Services Citizen Board for a one-year term of office commencing July 1, 2026, and ending June 30, 2027; Karen Pillis as a member of the Youth Services Citizen Board for a three-year term of office commencing July 1, 2026 and ending June 30, 2029; Dawn Erdman as a member of the Board of Zoning Appeals for a three-year term of office, commencing January 1, 2027, and ending December 31, 2029; and Shamaill Ross as a member of the Roanoke Civic Center Commission for a three-year term of office, commencing October 1, 2026, and ending September 30, 2029. title: Planning Commission Work Session
text: Updated 10/23/26 FRANKLIN COUNTY ZONING ORDINANCE UPDATE DRAFT ARTICLE 3 – PERMITS & APPLICATIONS l MARCH 26, 2026 ARTICLE 3. PERMITS AND APPLICATIONS1 DIVISION 3-1. IN GENERAL.2 If an applicant seeks both an amendment to the Zoning Ordinance and a Special Use Permit for the same property, both applications may be made jointly and processed at the same time if the proposed amendment does not add a conditional use not previously permitted by the terms of this Ordinance. Section 3-1-1. Preapplication Meeting.3 Prior to the submittal of an application for a Special Use Permit, Zoning Text and/or Map Amendment (rezoning), or Conditional Zoning, or a Site Plan, a preapplication meeting must be held between the applicant and the Administrator, unless otherwise waived by the Administrator. During this meeting the applicant may submit a Concept Plan for preliminary review, comment, and recommendation by the Administrator. Section 3-1-2. Minimum Submission Standards. A. The Administrator shall establish minimum standards for submission requirements of all applications associated with the Zoning Ordinance. (1) Applications shall contain all information required to prove compliance with the minimum standards of the Ordinance, including, but not limited to: a. Written description of request and grounds for requesting; and b. Applicable district, use, and community design standards. B. Upon written request by an applicant, the Administrator may waive or modify a submission requirement(s) upon a determination that the information is not necessary to evaluate the merits of the application, such waivers or modiﬁcations are for application requirements only and do not include variances or modiﬁcations from Zoning District or Use Standards. C. Additional information may be required as deemed reasonably necessary by the Administrator. D. A fee shall be paid for the examination and approval or disapproval of every permit and application submitted. The fee shall be payable at the time of ﬁling to the Treasurer of Franklin County paid via the online permitting system in the amount required by a fee schedule adopted by the Board of Supervisors. Section 3-1-3. Online Forms. Applications for Subdivision Site Plans, Variances Appeals, Special Use Permits, Zoning Permits, Land Use Permits, or amendments to the Ordinance or Oﬃcial Zoning Map Amendment (rezoning) and any other request requiring action shall be made on forms provided by the County through the County's online permitting system. 1 Editor’s Note: This Article organizes all permit and application provisions in one place for improved referencing. 2 Editor’s Note: This Division is new and establishes general terms for the Article. 3 Editor’s Note: The County should consider if it wants to change this to require a preapplication meeting for Zoning Map Amendments, and for others to be optional. The planning commission decided to leave as drafted. Article 3 – Permits and Applications l Page 3-1 of 33 FRANKLIN COUNTY ZONING ORDINANCE UPDATE DRAFT ARTICLE 3 – PERMITS & APPLICATIONS l MARCH 26, 2026 Section 3-1-4. Ownership and Interests Disclosures. A. An applicant must disclose all equitable ownership of the real estate included in an application. In the case of corporate ownership, the name of stockholders, oﬃcers and directors shall be provided, and in any case the names and addresses of all of the real parties of interest in accordance with the Code of Virginia § 15.2-2289. B. Pursuant to the Code of Virginia § 15.2-2287 petitions brought by property owners, contract purchasers, or their agents, shall be sworn to under oath stating whether or not any member of the local Planning Commission or governing body has any interest in such property: (1) Either individually; (2) By ownership of stock in a corporation owning such land, partnership; (3) As the beneﬁciary of a trust; (4) As the settlor of a revocable trust; or (5) Whether a member of the immediate household or any member of the Planning Commission or governing body has any such interest. Sec. 25-789 Fee Schedule Section 3-1-5. Fees and Charges.4 A. The Board of Supervisors shall establish, by Ordinance, a schedule of fees, charges and expenses, and collection procedures for Zoning and Land Use Permits, Special Use Permits, variances, appeals, amendments, site plan reviews, and other matters pertaining to this Ordinance.5 B. The schedule of fees shall be available for inspection in the oﬃce of the Administrator and may be altered or amended by the Board of Supervisors by Ordinance amendment, as directed in Code of Virginia § 15.2-107. C. Delinquent Taxes and Charges.6 Pursuant to the Code of Virginia § 15.2-2286 (B), prior to the initiation of an application or appeal, the applicant and/or county shall produce satisfactory evidence that any delinquent real estate taxes, nuisance charges, stormwater management utility fees, and any other charges that constitute a lien on the subject property that are owed to the County, have been paid in full, unless otherwise authorized by the County Treasurer. (1) The above provision applies only to the property or properties for which the application is attached. (2) If an applicant is the renter of a subject property and said property has associated unpaid taxes and fees owed to the County, the property owner(s) shall be responsible for paying those balances in full. 4 Editor’s Note: This section replaces and expands upon existing Section 25-789. Editor’s Note: It is recommended that the County establish a fee schedule outside of the Zoning Ordinance in order to amend it when needed without necessitating amendment of this Ordinance. 6 Editor’s Note: The content in C. is new, per Code of VA. 5 Article 3 – Permits and Applications l Page 3-2 of 33 FRANKLIN COUNTY ZONING ORDINANCE UPDATE DRAFT ARTICLE 3 – PERMITS & APPLICATIONS l MARCH 26, 2026 Sec. 25-147 Utility-scale solar generation facility D. In situations where the Administrator anticipates expenses for professional services related to review of an application that will exceed the amount recouped by the imposition of standard fees, the County shall require the applicant to pay the cost of the professional review service.7 (1) Examples of projects for which a deposit may be warranted include (but are not limited to) rezoning requests, planned development districts, and Special Use Permits that require professional review Comprehensive Plan review. (2) The payment shall solely be applied to payment of professional services by engineers, attorneys, surveyors, architects, landscape architects, etc., that are speciﬁcally engaged by the County to consult directly on the applicant’s proposed project. (3) Payment is an express condition of the County’s determination upon the application. Payment does not guarantee approval of the application. Nor does payment create a client relationship between the applicant and the professional services provider. Section 3-1-6. Withdrawal of Applications. 8 Sec. 25-740 Withdrawal of petitions A. Any application ﬁled pursuant to Division 3-2 of this Article may be withdrawn upon written request by the applicant prior to the submission of any public hearing notice for advertisement; provided: (1) If the request for withdrawal is made after the notice of hearing is published, such withdrawal shall be only with the consent of whichever body has advertised the hearing; and (2) The same petition shall not be reconsidered within 12 months of the date of action, unless the respective body approving withdrawal speciﬁes that the time limitation shall not apply. Section 3-1-7. Reconsiderations. A. The following shall apply for all zoning text and map amendment; conditional zoning; special use permits; and variance applications: (1) If denied by the Board of Supervisors, then such application, or one substantially similar, shall not be reconsidered sooner than 12 months from the date of the previous denial. (2) If denied by the BZA, then such application, or one substantially similar, shall not be reconsidered sooner than 12 months after the previous denial. B. The limits on reconsideration shall not impair the right of either the Planning Commission or the Board of Supervisors to propose any amendment to this Ordinance on their motion at any time. DIVISION 3-2. ZONING TEXT AND MAP AMENDMENTS9 Section 3-2-1. In General. Pursuant to the Code of Virginia § 15.2-2286 (7) whenever public necessity, convenience, general welfare, or good zoning practice requires, the Board of Supervisors may, from time to time, amend, 7 Editor’s Note: Language from existing Section 25-147 is included here. Editor’s Note: From Section 25-740 of the existing ordinance. 9 Editor’s Note: This Division consolidates all zoning text and map amendment language in one place for ease of referencing. 8 Article 3 – Permits and Applications l Page 3-3 of 33 FRANKLIN COUNTY ZONING ORDINANCE UPDATE DRAFT ARTICLE 3 – PERMITS & APPLICATIONS l MARCH 26, 2026 supplement or change, by Ordinance, the boundaries of the Zoning Districts or the regulations established in this Ordinance. Section 3-2-2. Standards and Procedures. 10 A. Initiation of change. Pursuant to the Code of Virginia § 15.2-2286 (7) any amendment to this Ordinance or the Zoning Map may be initiated by:11 (1) Resolution of the Board of Supervisors. (2) Resolution of the Planning Commission; or (3) Application of the owner, contract purchaser with the owner’s written consent, or the owner’s agent, of the property proposed to be rezoned. a. The application shall be addressed to the Franklin County Board of Supervisors or Planning Commission, who shall forward such application to the Board of Supervisors. B. Zoning Map Amendments. Applications for Zoning Map Amendments, including Conditional Zoning requests, shall be made to the Administrator and accompanied by a Concept Plan as detailed in Division 6 Division 3-6 of this Article.12 (1) The Director of Planning and Zoning or designee will transmit the application and other information to any state, county, or other government agencies for review and comment, as appropriate. (2) After the application is determined to be complete, and all agency comments have been received, County staﬀ will provide comments in writing to the applicant so revisions can be made, if necessary the county will collect all comments from other agencies to be included in the staff report. The staff report will be emailed to the applicant(s) once the Planning Commission has received their packets. Any revisions can be made by applicant(s), if necessary. (3) The Director of Planning and Zoning or designee will prepare and submit a written staﬀ report to the Planning Commission on the proposed zoning map amendment. (4) A Site Plan is required as detailed in Division 6 Division 3-7 of this Article. C. Standards for review. (1) The application for a rezoning or Zoning Text Amendment shall be referred to the Planning Commission for public hearing and recommendation. The Planning Commission shall present their recommendation on the proposed ordinance or amendment, including the Zoning Map, to the Board of Supervisors for public hearing and action. No recommendation or action shall be rendered until public notiﬁcations and hearings have been conducted in accordance with Division 3-10 of this Article. 10 Editor’s Note: This section includes updated information from existing ordinance Section 25-732 and updated Code of Virginia references. 11 Editor’s Note: The current ordinance does not allow the Planning Commission to initiate a Zoning Map Amendment. BG recommends changing this as written in this section. Recommendation accepted. 12 Editor’s Note: The requirement for a concept plan has been applied to all zoning map amendments and consolidated in one place rather than stated in each of the planned districts and overlays sections. Article 3 – Permits and Applications l Page 3-4 of 33 FRANKLIN COUNTY ZONING ORDINANCE UPDATE DRAFT ARTICLE 3 – PERMITS & APPLICATIONS l MARCH 26, 2026 (2) The Planning Commission shall advise the Board of Supervisors of their recommendation within 100 days from its ﬁrst meeting following the referral of the application. If after 100 days no recommendation has been made, the governing body shall assume that the Planning Commission concurs with the applicant and supports the amendment. The Board of Supervisors shall thereafter take any action it deems appropriate, unless the applicant requests an extension for a deﬁned period not to exceed a total of 90 calendar days13 from the date of the public hearing. (3) All motions, resolutions, or applications for amendment to the Zoning Ordinance and/or Zoning Map shall be acted upon, and a decision made within such reasonable time as may be necessary which shall not exceed 12 months unless the applicant requests or consents to action beyond such period or unless the applicant withdraws his motion, resolution, or application for amendment to the Zoning Ordinance or map, or both; otherwise, the amendment shall be deemed approved. a. In the event of and upon a withdrawal by the applicant, processing of the motion, resolution, or petition shall cease without further action as otherwise would be required. Sec. 25-733 Proffers and conditions, Sec. 25-734 Effect of conditions D. All changes aﬀecting the Zoning Map that are approved by the Board of Supervisors shall be entered onto the oﬃcial Zoning Map within 60 days following the approval of such changes. DIVISION 3-3. CONDITIONAL ZONING AND PROFFERS14 Section 3-3-1. Purpose and Intent. 15 Conditional Zoning provides a method for permitting the reasonable and orderly development of land through Zoning Map Amendments with reasonable conditions governing the use and development of such property. As authorized under the Code of Virginia §§ 15.2-2296 through 15.2-2303.3, reasonable conditions may be voluntarily proﬀered for the protection of the community when combined with existing Zoning Ordinance district regulations. The exercise of authority shall not be construed to limit or restrict powers otherwise granted nor to aﬀect the validity of any Ordinance adopted by the locality which would be valid without regard to this Division. In addition, the provisions of this Division shall not be used for the purpose of discrimination in housing. Section 3-3-2. Standards and Procedures. 16 Sec. 25-735 Zoning map notation not included A. Proﬀers of conditions; standards of consideration. 13 Editor’s Note: 13 “calendar days” changed to “days” per Planning Commission worksession on Feb. 24, 2026. text: Department of Planning & Community Development Franklin County Planning Commission Agenda November 10, 2026 I. Call to Order II. Roll Call III. Approval of Minutes from October 13, 2026, Meeting IV. APPLICATION for SPECIAL USE PERMIT – Application of Stanley Jones, Applicant, and Elemental Science Educational Support LLC, Owner, requesting a special use permit on an approximate 1.98 acres of property zoned A-1, Agricultural District. The parcel is located at 55 Woodman Road in the Union Hall Election District of Franklin County and further identified by real estate records as Tax Map/Parcel #0540007800. The purpose of this special use permit is to remove conditions two (2) (condition requiring adherence to VDOT regulations for the entrance) and four (4) (condition requiring approvals and permitting from zoning, building, E&S control, and storm water management) and modify condition five (5) (condition requiring adherence to perimeter landscaping) from Resolution #07-07-2026 approved by the Board of Supervisors on July 21, 2026 for school (public and private). This property has a future land use designation of Low Density Residential - County (SPEC-26-10 #0510007800) a. b. c. d. Staff Presentation (Tina Franklin) Applicant Presentation Citizen Comment Planning Commission recommendation for action V. Open Citizen Comment VI. Zoning Ordinance Update Work Session – Article 3 (tentative) VII. General Announcement and Updates VIII. Adjourn *** The Planning Commission’s next site visits are scheduled for December 2, 2026. Department of Planning & Community Development A meeting of the Franklin County Planning Commission was held on Tuesday, October 13, 2026 in the Board Room located at the Franklin County Government Center. THOSE PRESENT: Ron Jefferson – Vice Chair, Gills Creek District David Pendleton – Blackwater District C.W. Doss – Blue Ridge District Addison Hancock – Snow Creek District Matthew Peters – Boone District OTHERS PRESENT: Lisa Cooper – Planning Director Jenn Richardson – Clerk Tina Franklin – Planner II Haskell Brown, III – County Attorney THOSE ABSENT: Victor Evans – Chair, Union Hall District David Clements – Rocky Mount District Chris Dadak – County Attorney Vice Chair Jefferson called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m. Mr. Jefferson asked if the Planning Commission had any comments or changes to the September 8, 2026 minutes. There were no changes requested. The minutes were approved as written. Mr. Jefferson introduced the next item on the agenda: APPLICATION for SPECIAL USE PERMIT – Application of David and Jill Wood, Applicants and Owners, requesting a special use permit, on an approximate 2 acres of property zoned R2, Residential Suburban Subdivision District. The parcel is located at 201 Hampton Drive in the Union Hall Election District of Franklin County and further identified by real estate records as Tax Map/Parcel #0520109700. The purpose of this specialuse permit request is to allow for Home – Second single-family detached dwelling on a lot. This property has a future land use designation of Low Density Residential Department of Planning & Community Development – County and Lake Influence Area (0.5 mile buffer). (SPEC-26-6 #0520109700). Ms. Tina Franklin presented the staff report. She stated that the owners of the property currently occupy the existing dwelling which consists of a 2,000sf garage with 1,000sf living space including one (1) bedroom. She stated that the owners plan to build a new home for their occupancy, and the existing dwelling would be for an immediate family member. Ms. Franklin stated that according to the building department records, the certificate of occupancy for the existing singlefamily dwelling was issued for a two (2) bedroom home, however, the applicant’s/owner’s state the existing single-family dwelling would be a one (1) bedroom with an office and the new primary single-family dwelling would be four (4) bedrooms. She stated that the septic permit provided was approved for five (5) bedrooms by the Virginia Department of Health in March of 2025. Ms. Franklin stated that the proposed new dwelling is to be constructed behind the existing dwelling with the drain field lines located between the two (2) dwellings. Ms. Franklin stated that both dwellings would use the existing well and would share the upgraded septic system. She stated that surrounding lots on Hampton Drive were of various sizes. Ms. Franklin stated that the two lots that are zoned B-2 at the beginning of Hampton Drive were commercial businesses before the residential development on the remaining portion of the road. Ms. Franklin displayed four (4) GIS maps of the property and the concept plan. She stated that the conceptual plan submitted by the applicant showed the existing one (1) bedroom with the garage, the septic field with the drain lines, and the proposed new home closer to the lake. Ms. Franklin stated the proposed second dwelling on the property was allowed by a special use permit and this particular use would not be of a substantial detriment to adjacent properties due to the length of the property and the surrounding area being constructed with a mixture of single-family dwellings and manufactured housing existing or in the future. She stated that the property has privacy trees between the existing home and 235 Hampton Drive. Ms. Franklin stated that the second dwelling would generate similar amounts of noise and traffic as any other single residence. She stated that the use (second dwelling) would be in harmony with the purpose and the intent of this district because uses like single-family 2 Department of Planning & Community Development dwellings and manufactured housing are what is expected to be found in the R-2 zoning district. Ms. Franklin stated that the second dwelling for a family member would be seen as part of the neighborhood community and would not change the character of the district. Ms. Franklin stated that staff recommended that the Planning Commission recommend approval of the special use permit with the following four (4) conditions: 1. This special use permit authorizes only one second dwelling on Tax Parcel # 0520109700, and no additional residential dwellings shall be permitted on the property. 2. The second dwelling shall have its own address, clearly visible and displayed on the dwelling for 911 emergency services. 3. The applicant/property owner shall obtain all required permits from the Franklin County Building and Planning Departments prior to the use and occupancy of the second dwelling. 4. The applicant/property owner shall comply with all regulations per The Virginia Department of Health (VDH). Ms. Franklin asked if the Planning Commission had any questions for her. The Planning Commission had no questions for Ms. Franklin. Vice-Chairman Jefferson invited the applicant up to the podium to present. Mr. Wood stated that they were building a house closer to the lake and that they were going to use the existing one (1) bedroom for one of their older family members to potentially live in. The Planning Commission had no questions for Mr. Wood. Mr. Jefferson opened the opportunity for citizen comment. There were no citizens who signed up to comment on the application. Seeing none and hearing none, the opportunity was closed. Mr. Peters made a motion to approve the application with the four (4) conditions. Mr. Hancock seconded the motion. 3 Department of Planning & Community Development A roll call vote was conducted. The motion to approve the special use permit with the four (4) conditions recommended by staff, approved; 5-0-2-0 voting was as follows: AYES: Peters, Pendleton, Doss, Hancock, Jefferson NAYS: None ABSENT: Clements, Evans ABSTAIN: None Vice-Chairman Jefferson announced that the Board of Supervisors would hear this case on November 17, 2026. Mr. Jefferson introduced the next item on the agenda: APPLICATION for SPECIAL USE PERMIT – Application of Michael Hiles, Applicant and Owner, requesting a special use permit, on an approximate 8.13 acres of property zoned A-1, Agricultural District. The parcel is located at 4957 Webster Road in the Union Hall Election District of Franklin County and further identified by real estate records as Tax Map/Parcel #0460009108. The purpose of this special-use permit request is to allow for short-term tourist rental of dwelling. This property has a future land use designation of Low Density Residential – County and Lake Influence Area (0.5 mile buffer). (SPEC-26-7 #0460009108). Ms. Tina Franklin presented the staff report. She stated the property was located on a secondary state-maintained road, Webster Road (Route 655), and had a long driveway that circled around behind the home that would provide ample parking for the short-term rental. She stated that the water was supplied by private well and the sewer supply is a septic system. Ms. Franklin stated that the closest residence was approximately five hundred sixty-two (562’) feet from the proposed short-term rental location at 4957 Webster Road. She stated that the subject property was wooded on both sides of the property for adequate screening. Ms. Franklin stated that according to County records, the dwelling was a one-story single-family home constructed in 2025 and consisted of four (4) bedrooms, two (2) full bathrooms and a total living area of approximately 2,280 square feet. She stated that the septic permit was issued by the Virginia Department of Health in 2024 for a four (4) bedroom home. Ms. Franklin stated that the planning office had not received any information on the property manager’s contact. 4 Department of Planning & Community Development Ms. Franklin displayed four (4) GIS maps of the property and the concept plan. Ms. Franklin stated that the proposed short-term rental was located on a lot consisting of +/-8.130 acres, and the closest single-family dwelling was five hundred sixty-two (562’) feet. She stated that next to the property were single-family dwellings, vacant lots, and farmland. She stated that the surrounding properties had a variety of lot sizes with several properties being larger in size. Ms. Franklin stated that the property had a driveway leading to the dwelling off of Webster Road that is long and circled around behind the home that would provide ample parking for the short-term rental. She stated that the traffic generated by this shortterm rental would be similar to what is generated by a single-family dwelling with full-time residents. She stated that the noise of the rental should not be more than normally expected in a residential neighborhood. Ms. Franklin stated that the singlefamily dwelling could be rented to a maximum of eight (8) adults at this time. The septic permit that was issued by the Virginia Department of Health is for four (4) bedrooms. She stated that earlier in 2026 the Board of Supervisors approved a special use permit for the purpose of short-term rentals at 4984 Webster Road located across the street from this property short-term rental. Ms. Franklin stated that staff recommended that the Planning Commission recommend approval of the special use permit with the following five (5) conditions: 1. The special use permit authorizing the short-term rental dwelling on Tax Parcel #0460009108 shall only apply to the existing dwelling on the property. No additional dwellings on the property shall be used for a short-term rental unless this permit is revised by the Board of Supervisors after review and recommendation of the Planning Commission. 2. The owner shall always comply with the supplementary regulations for shortterm rentals found in Section 25-138 and Section 5.5-72 of the Franklin County Code. 3. The owner shall provide and maintain proof of liability insurance covering injury to a guest on the property of no less than $1,000,000. 4. The owner shall register the short-term rental use and shall have the property inspected for compliance with County Code. No short-term rental of the property shall be authorized until these inspections take place, and the property is found to be compliant with the applicable County Code. 5 Department of Planning & Community Development 5. The owner shall supply the Planning Department with the name and phone number of a property manager or contact person. The Planning Department shall be notified any time this information is changed. Staff will notify adjoining property owners of this information and notify them of any changes to this information. Ms. Franklin asked if the Planning Commission had any questions for her. The Planning Commission had no questions for Ms. Franklin. Vice-Chairman Jefferson invited the applicant up to the podium to present. The application was not present. Mr. Jefferson opened the opportunity for citizen comment. There were no citizens who signed up to comment on the application. Seeing none and hearing none, the opportunity was closed. Mr. Peters made a motion to approve the application with the five (5) conditions. Mr. Hancock seconded the motion. A roll call vote was conducted. The motion to approve the special use permit with the five (5) conditions recommended by staff, approved; 5-0-2-0 voting was as follows: AYES: Peters, Pendleton, Doss, Hancock, Jefferson NAYS: None ABSENT: Clements, Evans ABSTAIN: None Vice-Chairman Jefferson announced that the Board of Supervisors would hear this case on November 17, 2026. Mr. Jefferson introduced the next item on the agenda: APPLICATION for REZONE – Application of Christopher Bittinger, Applicant, and Dillon Docks Holding, LLC, Owner, requesting to rezone with possible proffers, an approximate 26.058 acres of property from A-1, Agricultural District, to B-2, Business District, General, to allow for contractors’ offices and facilities. The property is located at 521 Patience Lane in the Gills Creek Election District of Franklin County and further identified by real estate records as Tax Map/Parcel #0330001000. This property has a future land use 6 Department of Planning & Community Development designation of Low Density Residential – County and Lake Influence Area (0.5 mile buffer). (REZO-26-2 #0330001000). Ms. Tina Franklin presented the staff report. She stated that the purpose of the rezone was to allow for a contractor’s office and facilities in order to bring a longstanding dock construction business into compliance with the zoning ordinance. She stated that the existing business has operated on the property for nearly two (2) decades as commercial use. Ms. Franklin stated that the property was heavily wooded on all sides for adequate screening. She stated that a new building is proposed in the future for use with the business as shown on the conceptual plan. Ms. Franklin stated that the Planning and Community Development Department received a complaint about this business being operated on this property. If the rezone and special use permit is approved the property will be in compliance with the current zoning ordinance. She stated that the applicant/owner stated in their letter of application that they purchased the property and the dock building business in February 2026 from the previous owner in order to continue operating the dock building business in the same manner as it has been operated for nearly two (2) decades. Ms. Franklin stated that the applicant/owner indicated they are not introducing a new use to the property, but are continuing the legacy established by the previous owner and her husband who built a trusted business and strong relationships throughout the Smith Mountain Lake region and with neighboring property owners. She stated that the applicant/owner stated that their goal is to preserve and continue what they spent years creating while maintaining the same respect for the community and surrounding landowners. Ms. Franklin stated that there was no water or sewer on the property at this time, however private well and septic will eventually serve 521 Patience Lane. Ms. Franklin displayed four (4) GIS maps of the property, the concept plan, and an aerial image of the property. Ms. Franklin stated that there will be minimal noise from the dock building due to the work being done in the enclosed building. However, there should not be any more traffic along Patience Lane as there is now or has been because of the business. She stated that the private road had historically supported business 7 Department of Planning & Community Development operations without reported public roadway issues. The rezoning from A-1, Agricultural to B-2, General Business does not inherently intensify the use beyond existing levels. As far as environmental and site conditions, the ongoing use has not generated significant environmental concerns based on past county records. Ms. Franklin stated that adjacent residential uses are low-density and rural in nature. The existing business has coexisted with these uses for over two (2) decades without documented nuisance complaints. She stated that the only complaint of record on this business was filed this year in the Planning and Community Development office. Ms. Franklin stated that rezoning to B-2, General Business provides several public and administrative benefits such as the following: establishes clear compliance with the zoning ordinance, ensure business operations, structures, and future modifications meet full regulatory review criteria, and supports continued economic activity and employment. She stated that this business had not changed the character of the neighborhood, or increased traffic, noise, and strain on utilities or the environment over the last two (2) decades. Therefore, approving the rezone request would align the site with the zoning ordinance requirements, support continued operation of a long-standing business, and benefit the community. Ms. Franklin stated that staff concluded that the rezone from A-1, Agricultural to B2, General Business was consistent with and would be in harmony with the purpose and intent of the County Code and supported the Comprehensive Plan’s economic development and rural compatibility goals, formalizes an existing commercial use with no significant change in land-use impact and maintains compatibility with surrounding rural residential properties. Ms. Franklin stated that staff recommend that the Planning Commission recommend approval of the rezone from A-1, Agricultural, to B-2, General Business District, with the following one (1) proffer: 1. The property shall be developed in substantial conformance with the concept plan titled “Reba Dillon, prepared by owner, and dated September 3, 2026.” Ms. Franklin asked if the Planning Commission had any questions for her. Mr. Jefferson asked if the application requests a rezone of the full 26 acres. Ms. Franklin 8 Department of Planning & Community Development stated that the request is for 6.058 acres. There were no further questions for Ms. Franklin. Vice-Chairman Jefferson invited the applicant up to the podium to present. Mr. Chris Bittinger stated that he was the owner of Dillon Docks and Build SML. He stated that the company had been building docks in Franklin County for 20-25 years. Mr. Bittinger stated that the six (6) acres has two structures on it. He stated that he wanted to keep the surrounding area as agricultural. Mr. Bittinger stated that he submitted the request for rezoning because someone filed a complaint. He stated that he wanted to be in compliance. He stated that his main concern was the safety of his neighbors. He stated that his company has weekly safety meetings. Mr. Bittinger stated that the building of the docks happened on the lake. He stated that the company has three (3) work trucks that are used to transport tools and supplies to projects. King & Queen County Planning Commission Minutes October 6, 2026 The King & Queen County Planning Commission met on Tuesday October 6, 2026, at 6:00 p.m. in the King & Queen County Courts and Administrations Building in the Second Floor Conference Rooms A & B for their regular monthly meeting. Planning Commission Members Present: Mac Bradley Edmond Wilson, Jr. Hunter Richardson Robert Coleman, Jr. Barry Allen William Thomas Robert Shackelford Also in Attendance: Vivian Seay, County Administrator/County Attorney Donna Elliott Sprouse, Director of Community Development Resa Wilson, Multifunction Coordinator Lawrence Simpkins, Board of Supervisor Call to Order Chairman, Mr. Richardson, called the meeting to order. Roll Call/Determination of Quorum Ms. Wilson, acting secretary, took roll call and determined that a quorum was present. Approyal of Minutes September 1, 2026 After review of the September 1, 2026 minutes, a motion was made by Mr. Thomas to accept the minutes as presented, seconded by Mr. Allen. Voting For: Bradley, Richardson, Wilson, Thomas, Coleman, Shackelford Voting Against: None Abstain: Allen Citizens Comment Period- Planning Related Issues Only Mr. Richardson opened the floor for the citizen comment period. Page I of 4 Ann Ryland Glubiak, who lives at 4049 Canterbury Road, expressed support for the proposed tower after reviewing the revised plans. She also expressed appreciation for the process and the opportunity to work through concerns regarding the plans. Bette Albert, from the Walkerton area, expressed hope that the monopole design would become the standard for new towers in the future to help preserve the rural appearance of the County. Chairman Richardson closed the citizen comment period. New Business A. CBPA26-02 - Chesapeake Bay Exception & WQIA — Steve & Terry Stone (Set Public Hearing) Chairman Richardson introduced CBPA26-02, a Chesapeake Bay Exception and WQIA request for Steve and Terry Stone, involving tax map parcel #1624-54R-32I, located off Courthouse Landing Terrace in the Stevensville District. Mrs. Sprouse provided information regarding the request to construct a single-family dwelling on a pre-existing nonconforming lot. Mr. Thomas made a motion to set a public hearing for CBPA26-02 for November 2, 2026. Mr. Shackelford seconded the motion. The motion passed unanimously. Old Business A. CUP26-02 Conditional Use Permit — Clyde Scott Mitchell (Tax Map 32-53L-56) - New Verizon Communications Tower (Continued) Following deferral from the previous meeting, Chairman Richardson opened discussion of CUP26-02, a Conditional Use Permit request for Clyde Scott Mitchell involving tax map parcel #32-53L-56. Lisa Murphy, representing Vertical Bridge, reviewed the revised plans provided to Commission members. The proposed tower design was changed from a lattice tower to a monopole tower, and the proposed location was moved from the field farther back into the trees. Mrs. Sprouse reviewed the revised conditions, including the requirement for a self- supporting monopole tower. Where a 50-foot natural treed vegetation buffer around the fence is not provided, a four-foot strip of evergreen trees, seven feet in height at planting and spaced fifteen feet apart, would be planted and maintained around the exterior of the security fence throughout the term of the lease and/or completion of tower decommissioning, whichever is longer. The purpose of the rezoning is to allow the future development of approximately five to six detached single-family homes. Prepared and presented by: Allen Nicholls, Planning and Zoning Administrator ___ Application for Rezoning Case Number: RZ-09-26-01 Application Information Project Name: Bracqbien Rezoning Applicant: Karl and Gwen Bracqbien (property owner) Property Location: Portion of Tax Map 50-55 (Tax Map 50-55I) Total Parcel Acreage: 12.5 Acreage Proposed for Rezoning: 12.5 Zoning district: Agricultural (A-1) Proposed Zoning: Residential, Limited (R-1) Overview of Request The applicants propose to rezone an approximately 12.5-acre parcel on John Tucker Road from Agricultural (A-1) to Residential, Limited (R-1). The applicants’ stated intent is to subdivide the property into five or six residential lots of approximately two to 2.5 acres each and construct detached single-family homes. The proposed homes would be traditional, stick-built, single-story residences averaging approximately 1,200 square feet, with the possibility of attached one-car garages. The applicants Page 1 of 6 Return to Agenda have stated that the homes would be retained under common ownership and operated as longterm rental housing rather than sold as individual speculative homes or used as short-term rentals. The submitted conceptual plan illustrates both five-lot and six-lot development options. Under either option, three lots would be located along John Tucker Road. The remaining lots would be accessed through an existing 50-foot access easement along the eastern side of the property. No formal subdivision plat or site development plan is under review at this time. The current request is limited to a zoning map amendment. The submitted conceptual plan illustrates the applicants’ current intentions but does not establish the final lot configuration, entrance locations, drainfield locations, building locations, or development yield. Any future subdivision would be subject to the Madison County Subdivision Ordinance, Virginia Department of Health approval, Virginia Department of Transportation requirements, privateroad standards, applicable road-maintenance agreement requirements, and all other applicable regulations. The applicants’ stated intention to retain the homes as long-term rentals is also not, by itself, a restriction imposed by the requested R-1 zoning. Unless incorporated into an enforceable voluntary proffer or other legally acceptable restriction, the ownership and rental status of the future homes could change without an additional rezoning. Site and Surrounding Area The subject property is identified as Parcel X on a division survey dated June 4, 2026. The survey depicts Parcel X as containing 12.500 acres and being separated from a larger parent tract formerly identified as Tax Map 50-55. The subject property fronts John Tucker Road, identified on the survey as State Route 614 with a 40-foot right-of-way. The parcel has substantial frontage along John Tucker Road and also adjoins an existing 50-foot access easement recorded in Plat Book 41, Page 14. The property is identified by the applicants as vacant or in agricultural use and appears to consist primarily of open land with wooded areas along portions of its perimeter. The surrounding area is rural in appearance but contains an established pattern of single-family residential development. Nearby properties include agricultural parcels, individual residences, and the Sheffield Way residential subdivision. Residential, Limited (R-1) zoning and residential lots of a size generally comparable to those proposed are present in the surrounding area. The subject property is not served by public water or public sewer. Each future lot would therefore require an approved individual well and septic system, including adequate area for both a primary and reserve drainfield. The availability of suitable well and septic locations has not Page 2 of 6 Return to Agenda been established through the rezoning application and would be evaluated through the applicable Health Department and subdivision review processes. The conceptual plans show three proposed lots with access oriented toward John Tucker Road. Under the six-lot option, three additional lots would be served through the existing access easement. Under the five-lot option, two additional lots would use that access. Final entrance locations and configurations would be subject to VDOT and County approval. Procedural History & Public Notice Preliminary Development Review Committee A pre-application meeting was held at the July 7, 2026, meeting of the Preliminary Development Review Committee. Planning and Zoning Administrator Allen Nicholls recused himself from the Committee’s consideration of the case due to a close working relationship with the applicant. During this meeting, comments were made by stakeholders that included the following: VDOT: Matthew Mashhadi advised that, if the private-road entrance serves three parcels, the entrance would need to be constructed to VDOT low-volume commercial entrance standards. Final entrance design and permitting would be addressed during the subdivision and development process.. VDH: Emily Bourdon advised that the applicant would need to demonstrate adequate space for both a primary drainfield and a reserve drainfield for each proposed lot. Individual well and septic approvals would be required before development. Madison County Building Official: Jamie Wilks noted that the applicant is a County employee and stated that Mr. Wilks would personally handle the applicable official inspections and approvals to avoid the applicant’s involvement in the review of his own project. The Preliminary Development Review Committee recommended that the applicant submit a formal rezoning application for consideration by the Planning Commission. Planning Commission The rezoning application was received on August 20, 2026. First workshop: September 16, 2026. Second workshop: October 21, 2026 Advertising This public hearing was advertised in the Piedmont Journal Recorder the weeks of October 11, 2026 and October 18, 2026. Letters to adjacent and adjoining property owners were mailed October 9, 2026. Page 3 of 6 Return to Agenda Summary of Public Comment Written comment has been submitted by Mr. Troy Gooding. The letter is included in the information packet. Call to Order Determine Presence of a Quorum & Microphone Reminder Chairman Whitman determined there was a quorum.
