Midkiff Christopher C. King Susan M. Branscome Robert A. Epperson (via phone) Rodney S. Dunford Garry Rusty Beamer Heidi D. Lyall OTHERS PRESENT Matt Hankins, Deputy County Administrator Johnny Kincer, County Engineer Jesse Burnett, Ex-Officio Lisa Shelton, County Planner Andy Kegley DETERMINATION OF QUORUM AND CALL TO ORDER Chair Midkiff determined that a quorum was present and called the meeting to order. The Commission said the pledge of allegiance. CITIZENS’ TIME Chair Midkiff asked if anyone wished to address the Commission during Citizens’ Time. Hearing none, Chair Midkiff closed Citizens’ Time and proceeded with the agenda. APPROVAL OF MINUTES A motion was made by Mr. King to approve the September 1 & 28, 2026, minutes. The motion was seconded by Mr. Beamer and passed unanimously. SUBDIVISION ORDINANCE A. Minor Subdivision – The Commission reviewed a subdivision plat showing a minor subdivision approved by Mrs. Shelton for Irvin Holdings, LLC, Speedwell. B. Adjoining Owner/Lot Line Revision – The Commission reviewed a subdivision plat showing an adjoining owner/lot line revision approved by Mrs. Shelton for Ricky & Rhonda Jefferson and Melanie Jefferson, Fort Chiswell. C. Family Subdivision – The Commission reviewed two subdivision plats showing a family subdivision approved by Mrs. Shelton for Lester Bolt, Fort Chiswell and Ronald & Carol Hendrickson, Speedwell. COMING EVENTS The Board reviewed upcoming holidays and meetings for the month of October. October 5, 2026 Unapproved Minutes NEW BUSINESS Land Use Ordinance – The Commission discussed setting the public Hearing and Mr. Hankins went over a memo he had prepared of suggested dates, times and procedures: Mr. Epperson made a motion to hold the public hearing on October 26, 2026 at 6 p.m. at George Wythe High School Auditorium and to accept Mr. Hankins recommendations, as presented. Ms. Branscome seconded the motion, and the role call vote was as follows: AYES: David P. Midkiff Christopher C. King Susan M. Branscome Robert A. Epperson NAYS: None Rodney S. Dunford Garry Rusty Beamer Heidi D. Lyall COUNTY ENGINEER REPORT Mr. Kincer showed pictures of Lot 35 in Progress Park, spoke about how the construction was going and showed pictures of all the erosion and sediment control they have in place. EX-OFFICIO REPORT Mr. Burnett stated that he doesn’t have anything at this time. DEPUTY COUNTY ADMINISTRATOR REPORT Mr. Hankins stated that the County’s request for Federal money to help with a new cannery facility or the Lots Gap water project was not included in the budget. He also October 5, 2026 Unapproved Minutes stated that some of the fire fighters from Barren Springs along with two staff members from Administration is going to inspect the new Barren Springs fire truck in Louisiana next week. County staff met with VDOT staff to go over some potential projects in the county. Mr. Hankins gave an update on Citizens broadband. They are almost at the end of their project. They have to be done in 2026. Mr. Hankins talked about the animal shelter project and moving it to the Fairview site on the edge of the industrial park. COMMISSION CONCERNS Mr. King asked how the Autumn Blaze festival went at Rural Retreat Lake this weekend. Mr. Hankins stated that the rain hurt the attendance. Mr. Hankins stated that he was proud of his recreational staff. They pulled off a great “Liberty at the Lake” event and were well prepared for this event. He stated that maybe next year they will pull it back to a one-day event. Mrs. Lyall asked if there were plans to pave the gravel part out at Rural Retreat Lake because she saw paving equipment out there. Mr. Hankins stated that he was not aware of any plans to pave. He thought it might be road crews simply doing repairs. Mr. Midkiff asked what percentage or number of people in the county are still not served by broadband. Mr. Hankins reported that the county did not have those numbers. They have reached out to HCD to get numbers but have not received those yet. Ms. Branscome asked Mr. Kincer about the runoff at the solar farm. She stated that her nor her neighbor has heard back from anyone that they have tried to contact. She was wondering if Mr. Kincer could do a follow up with them. Mr. Kincer stated that DEQ and himself will be going out there tomorrow. Ms. Branson stated that someone from the Antique Tractor Club asked her about the County paying for all the utilities at the fairgrounds. Mr. Hankins stated that utilities were spelled out in their lease and if they didn’t have a copy of it, he would be glad to send them one. He also stated that he would reach out to Mr. Cassell and talk to him about this. Long term, the County may wish to take some of the land back to use it and there may be something they can do about the utilities. Mr. Dunford asked if there was any way to streamline the process of the meeting and instead of Mrs. Shelton reading each report on a subdivision she has done. Could the Commission look at them ahead of time, like they review the minutes, and if there are any questions, address those during the meeting. This would cut down on the meeting time. Mr. Hankins stated that as long as the requirements of the bylaws and the code are met, the Commission could certainly do that. Mr. Hankins and Mrs. Shelton will look into the this and let them know at the next meeting. ADJOURNMENT With no further business to transact, the Planning Commission adjourned at 6:51 p.m. until the Public Hearing on Monday, October 26, 2026, at 6:00 p.m. October 5, 2026 Unapproved Minutes ___ David Midkiff, Chair October 26, 2026 The Wythe County Planning Commission held a special called public hearing on Monday, October 26, 2026, at 6:00 p.m. in the George Wythe High School Auditorium, 1 Maroon Way, Wytheville, Virginia. MEMBERS PRESENT David P. Midkiff Christopher C. King Susan M. Branscome Rodney S. Dunford Gary Rusty Beamer MEMBERS ABSENT Robert A. Epperson OTHERS PRESENT Stephen D. Bear, County Administrator Matt Hankins, Deputy County Administrator Martha Collins, Clerk/Administrative Assistant Lisa Shelton, County Planner DETERMINATION OF QUORUM AND CALL TO ORDER Chair Midkiff determined that a quorum was present and called the meeting to order. LAND USE CLASSIFICATION ORDINANCE PUBLIC HEARING Chair Midkiff asked to hear from staff. Mr. Hankins stated that the Wythe County Planning Commission will conduct a public hearing Monday, October 26, 2026, at 6:00 p.m. to receive public comments on the proposed Land Use Classification Ordinance of Wythe County, Virginia. The hearing will be conducted in the auditorium of George Wythe High School, 1 Maroon Way, Wytheville, VA. Citizens will be heard in the order they are received. Due to anticipated number of speakers, the citizens speaking time will be limited to three (3) minutes per person. Advanced registration is available online until noon on the day of the hearing at www.wytheco.org/zoning and in person from 5:30 p.m. until hearing time. Alternatively, written comments for the record may be received via electronic mail to Lisa Shelton, County Planner, at ldshelton@wytheco.org or by mail at 290 South Sixth Street, Suite 350, Wytheville, VA 24382. This hearing is held in compliance with Section 15.2-2204 of the Code of Virginia. The proposed ordinance and zoning map may be viewed online at www.wytheco.ord/zoning or at Wythe County Administrator’s Office, 290 South Sixth Street, Suite 350, Wytheville, VA. By Order of the Wythe County Planning Commission, David P. Midkiff, Chair. Mr. Hankins started calling the speakers up in the order they were received. Bobbi Dillow-Walsh – “I’m Bobbi Dillow-Walsh. I am a lifetime resident of Wythe and Bland County. I've lived here in Wytheville, the town, for the past 15 years. I own two properties here in the town. I also serve as an HOA president for Green for the townhouses located behind Church Street, right in the historic district. So, I've owned October 26, 2026 Public Hearing Unapproved Minutes that property and have my mother living there now. So, I wanted to come and speak tonight. I have 25 years in power systems. First with, I recognize Dave from the years at ABB, Hitachi Energy. I've worked with Schneider Electric, the world's most sustainable company, and a publicly traded utility. And now with Siemens, and my role now within Siemens for the last year and a half has been that of our data center vertical, working with data center companies, developers across the country. So, living here in Wytheville and learning so much about what the county has been through and what the town is going through, it's mass opportunity and mass change, and I felt it pertinent to at least correlate what I've seen in those 25 years and what I've seen greatly in the last 5 to 10 years, and really speeding up the migration. And there are two points after reading your draft number four that jumped out at me that are not included in draft number four, and those two points are sustainability and agility. And if you don't remember anything else I say, because we've only got two minutes, just remember sustainability and agility, because the next stat that I wanted to share, due to the rapid growth of the industry, is expected to last. We know the AI movement will last for a while. We don't know how long it's going to last. A lot of folks expect this to be, a lot of companies are planning at least five years of this rapid, rapid growth. And again, that's just me and the industry, I'm not speaking on behalf of my current company in any capacity. It's just, this is just my comments. But over those five years, when the market does reach maturity, when AI reaches maturity, what the research shows is that the market will be left with at least 50 to 60% data center. That that is the expectation. So, consider this everything the way business is done to now. What the makeup of our MUSH market, your muni's, your utilities, your schools, the hospitals, they'll now be a category, very sizable category for data centers. So, back to sustainability. I know we don't have a sustainability group or effort or sustainability plan in Wythe County. Sustainability is basically our ability to, you know, weather any storm, to continue to grow, you know, to continue to make sure everybody has enough and is able to continue to grow economically, so doing this responsibly, I think we deserve to have each community deserves to have a sustainability plan. That's Wytheville, that's Fort Chiswell, that's Rural Retreat. I believe what we're missing there is a sustainability policy. Okay, thank you.” Mike Forrest – “I have only a couple comments. First and foremost, I am for planning, for zoning. I believe it builds a path that makes it better, easier to follow for the planning committee for industries coming to town. Secondly, there's 95 counties in the state. 8 of them, including Wythe County, do not have county-wide zoning. There's something got to be wrong if 92% of the counties have zoning and it's working for them. We need to have it too. That's all I have. Thank you.” Sarah Bates – “Hi, I’m Sarah Bates, and thank you for the opportunity to come and express my feelings. I want to start out by saying I feel frustrated and angry. I don't feel like you, as the Planning Commission, is really listening to those of us that have been most invested in coming to these meetings. One of the people I'm here with tonight lives on property where they've clearly expressed to you, they object to the designation for being ag land changed to being commercial. It's incredibly frustrating for them that they October 26, 2026 Public Hearing Unapproved Minutes overheard a member of the Board of Supervisors saying, ‘Well, it's money and power that brought that change.’ When we've been so clear, coming over and over, listening, watching you guys look parcel by parcel, but you aren't listening to those of us that feel like sustainability is broader than what you were just told. To me, sustainability is the ecology, the environment here, and this direction is already just adding to the damage we're all experiencing on Earth right now. I think it's time that everyone wake up and realize climate change is real, and we shouldn't be doing things to further it. We should be doing things to start to work to heal things, and I think it really matters in an agricultural county. So I'm angry, I'm frustrated, I'm trying to be calm and clear about it, but I don't feel like we are being heard as the regular people. If big money is running this, then you got it wrong in my mind. Thank you.” Donna Nichter – “Hi, Donna Nichter. I don't have a lot new to say. I think you've heard me say it before. I wasn't going to speak tonight, but I'm mad, so I decided to speak. I've been opposing data centers since last announced in December, and when we started Preserve Wythe, it was our understanding that zoning is the biggest way to stop any more from coming to Wythe County. At least at that point, we have public hearings, which are so well attended. The apathy in this county is disturbing. I started fighting for the entire county and then found out that it was actually in my backyard that I need to worry about in Whispering Pines. It was our understanding that agriculture would remain agriculture. I have cows up to my fence. I just have a small yard. It's not the best view in Wythe County, but it's sweet. That's why we bought there. That's why the whole neighborhood bought there. I listened to the conversation back and forth between the joint meetings, and there was a lot of ideas. You know, should we do this? Should we do that? Should we do this? But it was decided that the property right behind my fence, where the cows come up to, I talk to them, I sing to them, they're cool. All right. In front of my face on that big screen, it was changed from green to blue, right up to my fence. I'd like to know what that's going to do to my property values. I have no idea what they're planning on doing there. Maybe nothing, but I don't think it's going to help my property value. I was incensed when that was changed in front of my face. I've had so many conversations, so many emails. It felt like a gut punch. I would like to know how many of you, when you're looking at that map, actually know the areas that you're looking at, or do you just see colors? Seems to me that it comes down to quote ‘important families’, but we're all important, money, landowners, and cronies. That's a familiar history. That's all I got to say.” Hannah Ainsworth – “Hello, Hannah Ainsworth. I didn't plan on speaking tonight, so I'll keep it short. To be honest, I didn't really ever think about zoning that much until December 2025, which, when of course, was when the first data center was announced coming to our county, and as I shared, as I spoke at one of the county board meetings after that announcement, my immediate concern with that news was the recognition that inviting one in, rolling out the red carpet for one, whether that be in an industrial park or not, was rolling out the red carpet for across this county. We've seen it time and time again. We've seen it in Northern Virginia, where these data centers proliferate, and I'm October 26, 2026 Public Hearing Unapproved Minutes proud of our county. I love our county. My family has roots to this county for 200 some years. I live here and stay here because I love the region that we're in, and I think we need to preserve this region. I think you know, as zoning is a tool. I think it's important, and I support the use of zoning to protect this county and to give the public an opportunity to speak and give input on what should and should not come to our area. I won't go into a lot of the data center information. I've talked at a couple of the county board meetings. A lot of others have spoken about the harms and concerns there. I would encourage anyone who hasn't watched some of those to go back and watch them. And yeah, so that's it. I'm very supportive of any tool that this county has to keep data centers out. Thank you.” Rusty Jones – “I’m Rusty Jones. I live on the edge of the county. We're on the edge of the town, just adjacent to the county on Reed Creek. I have a 60-acre farm that we live on. I want to just say straight up front, I support what you are doing, I think we need zoning in this county. We've needed it a long time. I appreciate the work of the planning commission. Y'all put a lot of work into this, and I think you kind of gone unthanked for it. And I appreciate all the work y'all done. But I've lived on my farm, well, I've owned it for 20 years, and I'm zoned agriculture in the town because we have zoning. I've got a lot of friends that are farmers. You know, I've done taxes for people over the years and other things, so I know a lot of people in this county, and I know what their fears are of zoning, and what they're afraid of. And I wanted to speak tonight just to alleviate some of their fears. You know, I farm happily inside the town limits of Wytheville, zoned, and it works. You know, I've made a few changes to my property over the years. I've sold off a little bit and gone through some of the zoning processes to do that. Changed some property lines around, and if you give it a chance, I think you'll like it because in the end, I trust my neighbors more than I trust the governor, and more than I trust the president, or Congress, or the House of Representatives, or perhaps even the Board of Supervisors. You know, I mean, a group of my neighbors I believe I can come talk with about what we think would be the best things for Wythe County, and I think as neighbors we all listen to each other. So, it's been a long time coming. And all I wanted to say was, I thank the people that have brought us to this point, and I hope the people that need to … now? I've got a sister-in-law, and her granddaughter lives in South Boston. They have a data center right now, right now, their fish are dying in the river because there's not enough October 26, 2026 Public Hearing Unapproved Minutes
